newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Petroplus buys German, Dutch storage. [CORRECTED 18:08 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Petroplus buys German, Dutch storage. [CORRECTED 18:08 GMT]

text.p: Petroplus International BV said on Friday that it had taken over a total 156,000 cubic metres of storage capacity in Germany and the Netherlands.

The acquisitions include 65,000 cubic metres of capacity in Dortmund, 56,000 cubic metres in Neuss, Germany, from Paktank, a subsidiary of Pakhoed and 35,00 cubic metres in Dordrecht, the Netherlands, from Dutch oil trading company Frisol.
"Thanks to these acquisitions, Petroplus can expand its activities in storing mineral oils, chemicals and edible oils," the company said in a statement.
The acquisitions increase the storage capacity of the Petroplus group by 45 percent. The group has others sites in Germany as well as storage capacity in the Netherlands and Denmark.
Petroplus owns all of Vanol Mineralproduktie.
(Corrects headline and final paragraph to make clear Vanol does not own, but is owned by, Petroplus).
